newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia calls for China action on HK elections.
newsitem.headline: Australia calls for China action on HK elections.

text.p: Australia on Sunday called on China to ensure swift elections for a new Legislative Council for Hong Kong when it resumed sovereignty of the British colony on July 1 next year.

China on Saturday announced a new legislature to replace Hong Kong's elected assembly when British rule ends, a move Britain and the United States have described as contrary to promises to preserve Hong Kong's democratic rights.

Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said it was disappointing that China and Britain were not able to agree that Hong Kong's current Legislative Council serve its full four-year term, ending in 1999, and that China had thought it necessary to establish a Provisional Legislature.

"In the Sino-British Joint Declaration on Hong Kong (1984) and its own Basic Law for Hong Kong (1990) -- which will serve as Hong Kong's post-1997 constitution -- China has undertaken to provide an elected Legislative Council in Hong Kong," Downer said in a statement.

"The Australian government considers it important that the Provisional Legislature should exist for as short a time as possible and that elections for a Legislative Council be held as soon as possible after the transfer of sovereignty on 1 July 1997."

Australia considered the maintenance and development of democratic political institutions were important factors in Hong Kong's continued success as an international business centre, which was important to Australia's substantial interests there and in the Asian region, he added.
